clue.text: Relieving irritation by deciding not to compete

definitions.meaning: easing an itch by rubbing it with the nails
withdrawing a horse or player from a race or match

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is rubbing an itchy patch of skin; the other is pulling out of a contest before it starts.

clue.text: Pass a note which is far from friendly

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
D is a note in the musical scale

explanation.surface: Handing over a message that is decidedly unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like a verb, hand over, but it is a gap between mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold manner is chilly and distant, the opposite of warm and welcoming.

parts.note: cove is old slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: An Italian man's holiday break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recess' suggests a break from work, but it means a nook in a wall; COVE is old British slang for a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess set back into the wall of a room.

clue.text: Scuttle off to get some meat

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or rotten, so the letters of the first word are reworked

explanation.surface: Hurry away to fetch some meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the letters of SCUTTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutlets are small chops of lamb, veal or pork, so they are pieces of meat.

definitions.meaning: to smooth clothes with a heated flat appliance
a golf club with a metal head

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is smoothing creases out of laundry; the other is a type of golf club.

clue.text: Top man putting points in large assembly

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places the compass letters inside the rearranged word
putting one thing in another places the compass letters inside the rearranged word
assembly means putting parts together in a new order, so the letters of large are rearranged

parts.note: N and E are compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: The boss makes points at a big meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges LARGE to GERAL, and 'putting ... in' places NE inside it after GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A general is the most senior army officer, the man in overall command.

parts.note: man means a person, a human being
age is taken as written
able means capable or competent

explanation.surface: Someone past retirement age who is capable and obliging.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces simply follow on: MAN, AGE, ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Manageable means easily controlled or handled, so docile and obedient.

clue.text: A president not up to cleaning up

parts.note: washing is cleaning, as in washing up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word not is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: not is taken as written

explanation.surface: A head of state who is not able to do the washing-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not up' turns NOT into TON, and 'to' joins it after WASHING.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington was the first President of the United States.

clue.text: Facts an American lawyer put to certain soldiers

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: A US attorney lays the evidence before a group of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put to' just joins the two pieces side by side; the TA is Britain's part-time army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are pieces of information, the facts gathered for study.

parts.note: a slow-growing tree on the surface, but read as a tree that grows a fruit whose name sounds like slow: the sloe

explanation.surface: A remark about a healthy tree that grows slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'healthy', but it says the fruit's name is heard as 'slow': the sloe, which grows on this thorny shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackthorn is the hedgerow tree whose bitter fruit is the sloe.

clue.text: Maybe she can raise money on assets

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged some other way, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: Perhaps a woman is able to borrow against what she owns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges the six letters of SHE CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To encash is to convert something into cash, turning holdings into ready money.

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
sects are factions or parties within a larger body

explanation.surface: Tall people throwing elegant gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footers' suggests tall people, but it means creatures with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects all have six legs, so they are literally creatures with six feet.

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means shape, so the letters of the two words are moulded anew

explanation.surface: The Conservatives govern without making up their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' rearranges the ten letters of TORIES RULE; Tories are Britain's Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Irresolute means wavering and unable to make up one's mind.

definitions.meaning: one who ponders or theorises, from speculate meaning think
one who takes risky bets on markets or property

explanation.definitionFit: To speculate is both to muse on something and to invest riskily, so the noun covers a thinker and a risk-taker.

clue.text: Scorch round the motorway and mark results

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for scorching encloses the motorway letter

parts.note: to sear is to burn or scorch the surface
M stands for motorway, as in the M1, a British main road

explanation.surface: Burning rubber around the M25 leaves marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'results' only link the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A smear is a dirty streak or smudge, a mark left on a surface.

parts.note: pat means glib or slick, as in a pat answer
a tern is a seabird, a creature with wings

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking footballer on the wing teams up with a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a footballer playing out wide, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a template or exemplar to copy, the same as a model.

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft
lace is a fine openwork fabric

explanation.surface: Notice some soft, fine fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a verb, notice, but it is a noun, a location.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a particular location, the same as a place.

clue.text: Find a buyer for about a thousand, showing sense

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for selling goes round the thousand

parts.note: to find a buyer for goods is to sell them
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone sells something for about a thousand pounds, showing good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'roughly', but it puts SELL around M.
explanation.definitionFit: Smell is one of the five senses, alongside sight, hearing, taste and touch.

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the four letters of the following word are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone was sorry for having been terribly impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges the letters of RUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to feel sorry for it, so the past tense means felt sorrow over.

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln, the US president
the letter T is given as written

explanation.surface: Back Lincoln exactly, to a T.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a T' reads as 'exactly', but 'to a' only joins ABE to the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage someone, usually in wrongdoing.

parts.note: arch means principal or chief, as in archenemy

explanation.surface: A main tree stands to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The larch is a conifer that sheds its needles in winter.

parts.note: lean means thin or skinny

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the word for leftist is read in reverse

parts.note: a red is a communist or left-winger

explanation.surface: A thin, backward-looking radical worships a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressive' turns RED into DER. In Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to see his love Hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander was the lover of Hero, the priestess in the Greek legend, so her devoted suitor.

clue.text: Transport raising a laugh out East

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A vehicle getting chuckles in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges A LAUGH, and E is added after it; 'raising' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Haulage is the business of carrying goods by road, the transport of freight.

definitions.meaning: one who plumbs, measuring the depth of water with a weighted line
more sound, that is healthier or in better condition

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a device or person measuring sea depth; the other is the comparative of sound meaning healthy.

parts.note: astern means at or towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A choice between something Asian and something from England's past.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern both describe things from the East, especially Asia.

definitions.meaning: the retinue or entourage trailing behind a dignitary
points a weapon or camera at a target

explanation.definitionFit: A train is a line of attendants; to train a gun is to point it at something.

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field, a poetic word
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: A boring piece of agricultural research.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden means heavy and lifeless, as grey as lead, hence dull.

parts.note: sounds like calm after anxiety, but describes a bill that is no longer outstanding

explanation.definitionFit: An unsettled account is unpaid, so one no longer unsettled has been cleared by payment.

clue.text: Overcome in a most unlikely manner

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words most unlikely, across the break between them

explanation.surface: Defeated in the least probable way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a ... manner' frames the words; the run sits across mo-ST UN-likely.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to daze or overwhelm them, as a blow does.

indicators.note: make here means build a new arrangement out of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Playwrights who drive painters crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges the ten letters of ARTISTS and MAD together.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatists are playwrights, people who write for the stage.

clue.text: Heartless sailor having to retreat a pace

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word for sailor is removed

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: retreat means go backwards, so the little word to is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A cruel sailor has to back off by one step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes the A from TAR, leaving TR; 'retreat' turns TO into OT, and 'having' just joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A trot is a gait of a horse, a pace between a walk and a canter.

clue.text: Setting right on the matter of fertiliser

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters
a dressing is manure or compost spread on soil

explanation.surface: Correcting a document about manure.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to put it right or remedy it.
